title: ‘Clearly not working’: Sam Altman hits AI industry over political spending
source_used: Townhall relay of Politico's exclusive Decoded interview (https://townhall.com/news/jeff-charles/2026/10/05/sam-altman-blasts-political-spending-in-ai-industry-n2684119); its opening paragraphs carry Politico's own wording, its later paragraphs are Townhall commentary and were not used
key_facts: Politico's Brendan Bordelon interviewed OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman in an exclusive marking the launch of Decoded by POLITICO.
Politico says Altman admits 'something's clearly not working' with the artificial intelligence money that has flooded the midterm elections.
Politico says Altman does not expect President Donald Trump's rebrand of the technology to improve the industry's image with the American public.
Altman: 'I get why AI has a really negative perception right now' and 'I don't think spending money on politics is what's going to make people feel better about it.'
Altman: 'The industry needs to figure out a way to address what the actual concerns are, and right now, a lot of people in the industry are being quite tone deaf.'

In the same interview Altman said OpenAI is more tolerant than rival Anthropic of less-than-catastrophic harms from AI, linking them to 'the lighter touch regulatory stance that we advocate for' (the part carried in our 5 Oct edition).
quote_evidence: “I get why AI has a really negative perception right now,” Altman told Brendan Bordelon in an exclusive interview marking the launch of Decoded by POLITICO.
“I don’t think spending money on politics is what’s going to make people feel better about it.
The industry needs to figure out a way to address what the actual concerns are, and right now, a lot of people in the industry are being quite tone deaf.”
why_it_matters_hint: The head of OpenAI publicly doubts that the AI industry's political money is improving its image, in the middle of the midterm elections.
event_date: Politico exclusive published 5 Oct 2026 (Decoded launch interview; first Politico story from it ran 4 Oct)
notes: Politico's page returned 403. Read through Townhall's relay of Politico's wording; the original was not seen, so the status is REPORTED (one outlet). Same interview as 5 Oct edition item 96, different remarks (political spending). Vanity Fair's Part 2 interview (5 Oct) has its interviewer saying it was reported that OpenAI president Greg Brockman backed out of a $25 million pledge to the Leading the Future super PAC; not used in the entry.
